name: Future Garage
summary: 2-step garage filtered through Burial: hits placed by ear off the grid, rimshots, congas and clicky found sounds where a snare should be, and percussion treated as texture under rain and vinyl crackle. Velocity is fragile and constantly moving, hats are sparse and silence is structural.

sounds.kick: Rounded, soft-attack kick with a clicky hat layered for presence; low in the mix and never loud enough to break the mood.
sounds.snare: Reverbed rimshot paired with a short spritely snare, or 'blocky, wooden' found-sound clicks; snare triples (ghost-then-accent) instead of flams.
sounds.hats: Two very short hats (one closed, one slightly open) at low velocity, swung 55–65% or nudged off-grid by hand.
sounds.percussion: Congas, bongos, clave-like ticks, finger clicks, lighter flicks, video-game FX; a heavily reverbed 'big perc' filling the empty final beat.
sounds.cymbals: None as such — crackle, rain and reversed reverb tails do the cymbal's job.

machines: Roland TR-808 / TR-909 / LinnDrum rimshots — the backbone click (owned)
Roland CR-78 / Korg Minipops — soft woody clicks and brushes (owned)
Akai S900 / MPC60 — 12-bit resampling of found sounds (owned)
Breakbeat libraries — Amen/Think slices at low velocity for ghost skips (owned)
Sony Sound Forge grid-less workflow — Burial's actual tool; emulate with quantize off (get elsewhere)
Field recordings, vinyl crackle, rain and game-sound libraries (get elsewhere)
